mission_09: Nested cross-validation provides an unbiased estimate of model performance when hyperparameter tuning is involved. The outer CV loop splits data into training and test folds, while the inner CV loop performs hyperparameter tuning on each outer training fold. This separation ensures that the test fold in the outer loop has never been used for any aspect of model selection, providing a truly unbiased performance estimate. Non-nested CV, where tuning and evaluation share the same folds, produces optimistically biased estimates because the same data influences both hyperparameter selection and performance measurement. The difference between nested and non-nested estimates quantifies the degree of overfitting to the validation set. Nested CV is the gold standard for performance estimation in research and should be used whenever reporting final model performance.
